concept_text_structured.intro: The RELATE Framework gives underwriters a structured way to use AI for customer communication drafts that stay professional, policy-aligned, and relationship-preserving. It acts as a constraint checklist to prevent AI from producing output that is either defensively vague or dangerously specific.

cards.title: Recognize
cards.body: Acknowledge the customer's concern and emotion without admitting fault or liability. This validates their experience while maintaining legal and policy boundaries.

cards.title: Explain
cards.body: State facts and reasoning in plain language, free of internal jargon. Provide context at the right level of detail to help the customer understand the decision.

cards.title: Limit
cards.body: Be explicit about what can and cannot change, and why, at a high level. Give the customer clarity on the boundaries of the situation.

cards.title: Alternatives
cards.body: Offer two or three concrete next steps the customer can actually take. Provide a clear path forward rather than a dead end.

cards.title: Tone
cards.body: Write as a professional peer, not as a gatekeeper. Maintain a respectful, collaborative voice that preserves the relationship.

cards.title: External
cards.body: Never allow internal risk codes, committee names, system identifiers, or non-public rationale to appear in customer-facing output. This acts as a disclosure firewall.

guardrails: Do not admit fault or liability when acknowledging customer concerns
Avoid internal jargon and system-specific language in customer communications
Never expose internal decision logic, risk ratings, or committee reasoning to customers
Ensure all next steps offered are concrete and actionable for the customer
Maintain professional peer tone rather than authoritative gatekeeper tone

good_example_structured.scenario: Draft a customer response to someone upset about their credit limit reduction.
good_example_structured.before_prompt: Draft an email to a customer upset about their credit limit reduction.
good_example_structured.before_issue: The prompt lacks structure and guardrails, resulting in output that reveals internal processes and risk language that could escalate customer frustration.
good_example_structured.after_prompt: Draft a response to a customer upset about a credit limit reduction. R: Acknowledge frustration and take concern seriously—do not admit fault. E: Explain periodic review identified working capital volatility; we want to ensure sustainability. L: State reduction stands today but is not permanent. A: Offer two options: (1) submit updated financials for re-review, or (2) explore seasonal restructuring. T: Professional peer tone—direct, warm, no jargon. E: Exclude internal risk codes, committee names, system names, or non-public rationale.
good_example_structured.after_benefit: The RELATE structure ensures the response acknowledges emotions, provides clear rationale, sets boundaries, offers actionable next steps, and maintains appropriate tone while protecting sensitive internal information.
good_example_structured.outcome: A warm, professional response that addresses customer concerns, preserves the business decision, and opens constructive paths forward without revealing internal processes or admitting fault.

anti_pattern_structured.headline: Exposing Internal Scoring Logic to Customer
anti_pattern_structured.failure_scenario: An underwriter pasted an entire internal Teams thread containing sensitive risk rating scores and committee thresholds directly into an AI prompt, asking it to draft a customer-facing reply. The AI incorporated these internal details verbatim into the response, revealing the existence and mechanics of the scoring system to the customer.
chain: Customer discovers internal scoring system and feels judged by opaque algorithm
Customer escalates concern to legal team
Formal complaint filed and relationship breakdown occurs
Potential regulatory disclosure incident and reputational damage
anti_pattern_structured.root_lesson: Always apply the External-only filter before passing any content to AI: strip internal notes, thresholds, scoring logic, and colleague commentary. Only include information appropriate for the customer to see, and verify the AI output contains no sensitive internal details before sending.

takeaway_structured.statement: Embed RELATE as a six-point constraint in every AI prompt for customer communication, and you turn a high-friction message into a professional, relationship-preserving conversation that never leaks internal logic.

action_1.title: Build RELATE into prompt templates
action_1.body: Create a reusable AI prompt checklist that includes all six RELATE elements (Recognize, Explain, Limit, Alternatives, Tone, External only) and use it every time you ask AI to draft a customer response. This ensures consistency and prevents accidental disclosure of internal risk codes or decision logic.

action_2.title: Review AI drafts against RELATE criteria
action_2.body: Before sending any AI-generated customer communication, audit it against each RELATE element to catch vague language, jargon, or internal identifiers that could damage trust. Flag any draft that fails to offer concrete alternatives or that exposes non-public rationale.

concept_text_structured.intro: The Copilot Surface Selector is a decision tree that matches task type to the right surface across Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, and SharePoint. Using the wrong surface at the wrong moment creates audit gaps, confidentiality breaches, or rework.

cards.title: Collaboration
cards.body: Teams Copilot synthesizes deal threads, gathers context, or recaps stakeholder discussions. Risk is low if you abstract away client-specific identifiers before prompting.

cards.title: Respond
cards.body: Outlook Copilot drafts customer-facing communications. Risk is high — never paste internal credit notes, pricing rationale, or system-of-record data into a customer email draft.

cards.title: Author
cards.body: Word Copilot builds internal memos, decision rationale paragraphs, or coverage summaries. Medium risk — always verify figures against your source data before finalizing.

cards.title: Financial
cards.body: Excel Copilot analyzes variance tables, exposure summaries, or premium calculations. Low risk when you work only with data already in the workbook.

guardrails: Never use a general AI chat tool for underwriting work — only use Copilot surfaces governed by your organization's data policies
Practice safe chaining: when passing output from one surface to the next, verify at each handoff that internal-only content has not migrated into an external-facing document
Confirm access controls before sharing AI-assisted drafts on SharePoint
Abstract away client-specific identifiers before prompting in Teams
Never paste internal credit notes, pricing rationale, or system-of-record data into customer email drafts

good_example_structured.scenario: A customer care team needs to summarize internal discussions, draft underwriting decisions, and communicate coverage outcomes to a client while protecting confidential information.
good_example_structured.before_prompt: Summarize all messages about the coverage review and draft a customer email with all relevant details and pricing information.
good_example_structured.before_issue: This prompt risks exposing internal pricing, dollar figures, and confidential underwriting logic to the customer.
good_example_structured.after_prompt: Summarize the last 10 messages using only general terms (no dollar figures). Draft a professional customer email using only approved wording and calm-clear-next-steps structure. Do not include internal pricing notes.
good_example_structured.after_benefit: Explicit constraints and surface-specific prompts prevent confidential data leakage while maintaining clarity at each handoff.
good_example_structured.outcome: A secure multi-surface workflow that produces a clean internal summary, reviewed memo, and customer-safe email with access controls enforced.

anti_pattern_structured.headline: Unreviewed AI Output Sent to Customer
anti_pattern_structured.failure_scenario: An underwriter copied sensitive deal files into a public AI chat tool, then pasted the AI-generated output directly into a customer document without review or verification. The document was forwarded to the customer without any human validation or audit trail.
chain: No audit trail created distinguishing AI-generated content from verified information
Internal pricing logic and confidential credit notes exposed in customer-facing document
Action violates data governance policy and creates confidentiality breach
Organization faces compliance exposure and cannot demonstrate output was validated against system-of-record
anti_pattern_structured.root_lesson: Always review AI output against your system-of-record before sharing externally, maintain an audit trail of what was AI-generated versus human-verified, and never paste sensitive internal data into public tools without explicit governance approval.

takeaway_structured.statement: Always match the Copilot surface to the task and confidentiality level, and verify at every handoff that internal-only content has not leaked into external-facing outputs.

action_1.title: Select surface by risk level
action_1.body: Before using Copilot, identify whether your task is internal (Teams, Word, Excel, SharePoint) or external-facing (Outlook), and choose the appropriate surface. Never paste confidential data like credit notes or pricing rationale into customer-facing communications.

action_2.title: Audit content at each handoff
action_2.body: When moving output between surfaces—such as from a Teams recap into a Word memo or final Outlook email—pause and verify that internal-only identifiers, figures, and rationale have not migrated into external documents. This verification step prevents audit gaps and confidentiality breaches.

concept_text_structured.intro: The SIFT Variance Lens is a four-step discipline that keeps AI in the role of hypothesis generator and keeps you in the role of validator when analyzing financial variances. It prevents the most costly analytical error in underwriting: accepting the first plausible story.

cards.title: Select
cards.body: From the full variance output, identify the 3–5 swings that carry the most underwriting weight. Focus on variances that affect debt service capacity, covenant headroom, or collateral quality.

cards.title: Isolate
cards.body: For each selected variance, generate 2–3 plausible drivers and treat these as competing hypotheses, not facts. AI is excellent at producing this list quickly—but it cannot know which hypothesis is true without evidence.

cards.title: Find
cards.body: For each hypothesis, specify the exact data that would confirm or rule it out, such as price-versus-volume splits, input cost schedules, aged receivables detail, or management commentary. If the evidence isn't in the file, that becomes your next information request.

cards.title: Tie
cards.body: Once a driver is confirmed by evidence, map it to a concrete underwriting response—covenant adjustment, cash flow stress test, collateral review, or escalation.

guardrails: Separate what changed from why it changed from what you do about it—every time
Treat AI-generated hypotheses as competing possibilities, not conclusions
Require evidence before accepting any variance explanation
Focus only on variances with material underwriting impact

good_example_structured.scenario: An underwriter analyzes financial variances in a credit facility to determine appropriate covenant structures.
good_example_structured.before_prompt: The analyzer flags EBITDA margin down 180 bps and DSO up 22 days for Meridian Industrial Co. The underwriter notes 'margin pressure and slower collections' and drafts a tighter covenant package.
good_example_structured.before_issue: The response treats symptoms as root causes without isolating hypotheses or gathering evidence, leading to overly restrictive covenants that may not address the actual drivers.
good_example_structured.after_prompt: Select top variances (EBITDA margin −180 bps, DSO +22 days). Isolate hypotheses for each. Find evidence via cost-of-goods detail, one-time schedules, aged receivables, and customer contracts. Tie findings to targeted actions.
good_example_structured.after_benefit: The structured approach isolates root causes, gathers supporting evidence, and links findings directly to proportionate covenant design rather than blanket restrictions.
good_example_structured.outcome: A targeted, evidence-backed covenant structure (e.g., normalization for one-time charges and concentration covenants) instead of a blunt response to misread variances.

anti_pattern_structured.headline: Accepting AI Summary Without Source Validation
anti_pattern_structured.failure_scenario: The underwriter accepted the AI's margin compression explanation (rising steel costs) at face value without validating the underlying data or investigating alternative causes. The actual driver was a one-time inventory write-down, not commodity costs, making the AI hypothesis fundamentally incorrect.
chain: Irrelevant covenant added based on misdiagnosed risk driver
Normalized margin appears weaker than reality; deal pricing and terms misaligned with true credit quality
Underwriter forced to re-present corrected analysis to credit committee
Lost credibility, delayed approval, and undermined confidence in AI-assisted underwriting
anti_pattern_structured.root_lesson: Always validate AI summaries by tracing back to source data and investigating root causes independently before embedding conclusions into credit decisions. Never treat an AI hypothesis as confirmed fact without corroborating evidence from the underlying financials or borrower disclosures.

takeaway_structured.statement: SIFT turns AI-generated variance hypotheses into validated, evidence-backed underwriting decisions by forcing you to confirm the 'why' before you act on the 'what.'

action_1.title: Prioritize variances by underwriting weight
action_1.body: When reviewing AI variance output, immediately filter to the 3–5 swings that materially affect debt service capacity, covenant headroom, or collateral quality. Ignore line items that don't move the needle on credit risk.

action_2.title: Demand evidence before accepting hypotheses
action_2.body: For each plausible driver AI generates, specify the exact data needed to confirm or rule it out—then verify that evidence exists in your file before taking any underwriting action. If evidence is missing, make it your next information request.

concept_text_structured.intro: End-to-End AI Workflow Integration treats each stage of an underwriting case as a distinct checkpoint where AI assists and a human verifies before output moves forward. The six domains form a sequential chain that protects confidentiality, structures outputs, validates logic, ensures compliance, tests hypotheses, and manages tool selection and storage.

cards.title: SAFE
cards.body: Protects confidentiality by abstracting inputs before any prompt is written. This is the first stage where sensitive deal information is sanitized before entering any AI system.

cards.title: CRAF
cards.body: Structures every prompt with Context, Role, Action, and Format so outputs are usable. Applied across Teams Copilot, Word Copilot, and Word to ensure consistent, actionable AI-generated content.

cards.title: VERIFY
cards.body: Validates sources, recency, and logic before any output leaves your desk. Ensures logical consistency and that AI-generated narratives are not accepted at face value.

cards.title: RELATE
cards.body: Governs all customer-facing language for tone and compliance. Shapes internal recommendations into stakeholder communications that meet regulatory and brand standards.

cards.title: SIFT
cards.body: Tests risk hypotheses against evidence rather than accepting AI-generated narratives at face value. Stress-tests financial analysis and deal assumptions before recommendations are finalized.

cards.title: Surface Selector
cards.body: Ensures the right tool is used at the right stage and outputs are stored correctly in SharePoint or the credit system of record. Includes clear AI-assistance disclosure at filing.

guardrails: Sequential gating: no output from one stage becomes an input to the next until a human has reviewed it
Documentation is non-negotiable at every gate: record what was AI-assisted, what was independently verified, and what remains an assumption
Maintain judgment, accountability, and audit trail throughout the workflow
Preserve speed and consistency while ensuring human oversight at each checkpoint

good_example_structured.scenario: An underwriter must assess a marine equipment manufacturer deal and recommend a credit limit for an approval memo.
good_example_structured.before_prompt: Paste the full deal brief into Teams Copilot, ask it to 'assess the company and recommend a credit limit,' copy the output into the approval memo, and submit.
good_example_structured.before_issue: No source verification, unlabelled assumptions, and AI-generated figures are presented as fact without validation.
good_example_structured.after_prompt: Follow a 9-step workflow: (1) abstract sensitive data, (2) use structured prompts with explicit scope limits ('Using only the context below'), (3) verify each claim against external sources, (4) generate narratives only from verified data with instruction 'Do not infer causes not stated in the data,' (5) validate hypotheses with deal team and external sources, (6) draft recommendations with explicit instruction 'Do not add facts not present in the inputs,' (7) perform logic checks, (8) draft customer communication, (9) file with AI-assistance disclosure.
good_example_structured.after_benefit: Every claim is traceable to verified sources, assumptions are explicit, and the final memo is auditable with clear disclosure of AI assistance.
good_example_structured.outcome: A complete, defensible credit file with validated risk factors, verified financials, and documented reasoning that can withstand regulatory review.

anti_pattern_structured.headline: Unvetted AI Tool Data Dumping
anti_pattern_structured.failure_scenario: An underwriter pastes confidential client data—legal entity names, unaudited financials, internal credit discussions—into an unapproved public AI tool to accelerate deal analysis. The tool generates a confident recommendation that the underwriter submits with minimal review.
chain: Confidential client data is exposed outside approved systems, violating data governance and privacy policy
Output contains no source citations, making financial figures unverifiable and indistinguishable from hallucinations
Facts, assumptions, and recommendations are blended without labeling, destroying auditability and decision traceability
If the decision is challenged, the underwriter cannot demonstrate independent judgment or evidence chain, exposing the firm to regulatory and reputational liability
anti_pattern_structured.root_lesson: Always verify that the tool is approved for the data classification level, never paste confidential data into unapproved systems, and require all AI-assisted analysis to include explicit source citations, assumption labeling, and independent verification before submission.

takeaway_structured.statement: Integration is not about letting AI run the case — it is about using all six domains as sequential human-gated checkpoints so that every AI output is verified, labelled, and traceable before it drives an underwriting decision.

action_1.title: Review and gate each stage
action_1.body: Before passing any AI-assisted output to the next workflow step, pause to independently verify its sources, logic, and recency. Document what was AI-generated versus what you validated yourself.

action_2.title: Label and file with disclosure
action_2.body: When finalizing underwriting communications or storing outputs in SharePoint, explicitly mark which sections received AI assistance and maintain a clear audit trail of assumptions and human judgments. This preserves accountability and supports future review.
